answer.answer: The ST-EVA archive establishes that AAPL's revenue series (mapped from us-gaap:SalesRevenueNet) contains multiple unresolved ambiguities across many periods, not a single unexplained period. For numerous fiscal periods, the SEC XBRL endpoint returns different values for the same concept and period across different filings (original 10-K vs 10-K/A amendments, and later-year filings that restate prior periods). Examples include FY2007 ($24.006B vs $24.578B), FY2008 ($32.479B vs $37.491B), FY2009 ($36.537B vs $42.905B), Q3 2009 ($26.667B vs $30.698B), and Q4 2009 ($8.337B vs $9.734B). Every observation carries a PARTIAL mapping fidelity (not EXACT), series breaks labeled "NOT_EXPLAINED_BY_ST_EVA" for both the SalesRevenueNet→revenue and Revenues→revenue mappings, and an ambiguity field explicitly stating "NOT_EXPLAINED... the source endpoint aggregates dimension members without returning the member, so the aggregate is not identifiable from the evidence held." All observations are UNVERIFIABLE (single source, no cross-validation). The series is truncated at 200 of 339 points. The archive does not select a winner among competing values; it records them all with NO_WINNER_SELECTED.
uncertainties: Which dimension members (product lines, geographies, etc.) are included in each aggregated SalesRevenueNet value — the SEC API does not expose them.
Whether the restatements in 10-K/A filings reflect error corrections, accounting policy changes (e.g., ASC 606 adoption), or reclassifications — the filings' narrative disclosures are not in ST-EVA.
Which of the competing values for each period is the currently accepted figure per Apple's latest filing — ST-EVA does not apply a 'latest filing wins' rule.
The exact nature of the concept mapping break between us-gaap:SalesRevenueNet and us-gaap:Revenues — ST-EVA marks it NOT_EXPLAINED_BY_ST_EVA.
